summary: Preserve the case where super() returns a replacement object that becomes this for the derived constructor and receives derived instance fields.

target.notes: Use JavaScript-compatible Construct semantics so the value returned from the base constructor initializes the derived this binding; then initialize derived instance elements on that receiver.

caveats: A C# `: base()` call cannot replace the derived receiver object.
references: ECMAScript Super Calls and Super Property: https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-super-keyword

tests.name: base replacement becomes derived this
tests.input: class B { constructor(){ return {fromBase:true}; } } class D extends B { x=1; } const d=new D(); console.log(d.fromBase,d.x);

tests.name: edge: replacement may break instanceof D
tests.input: class B { constructor(){ return {}; } } class D extends B {} console.log(new D() instanceof D);
